# Query API reference

Call query API endpoints to execute query runs against your HCP Terraform workspaces. Query runs retrieve information about workspace resources and configurations. They are asynchronous operations that you can monitor for status and results.

## Overview

The scope of the API includes the following endpoints:

| Method   | Path                                              | Action                                                                                                     |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------- |------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `POST`   | `/queries`                                        | Call this endpoint to [create a query run](#create-a-query-run).                                          |
| `GET`    | `/workspaces/:workspace_id/queries`               | Call this endpoint to [list query runs for a workspace](#list-query-runs-for-a-workspace).                |
| `GET`    | `/queries/:query_id`                              | Call this endpoint to [show a query run](#show-a-query-run).                                              |
| `POST`   | `/queries/:query_id/actions/cancel`               | Call this endpoint to [cancel a query run](#cancel-a-query-run).                                          |


## Create a query run

This endpoint creates a new query run.

`POST /queries`

| Status  | Response                  | Reason                                                                |
|---------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [201][] | [JSON API document][]     | Successfully created a query run.                                     |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][] | Not found or the user is unauthorized to perform this action.        |
| [422][] | [JSON API error object][] | Malformed request body, such as missing attributes and wrong types.   |
| [500][] | [JSON API error object][] | Internal system failure.                                              |


### Request body

This `POST` endpoint requires a JSON object with the following properties as a request payload.

Properties without a default value are required.

| Key path                                          | Type    | Default          | Description                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------|---------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `data.type`                                       | string  |                  | Must be `"queries"`.                                                                                        |
| `data.attributes.source`                          | string  |                  | The source of the query. Use `"tfe-api"` for API requests. Query definitions come from the configuration version. |
| `data.attributes.generate-config-out`             | boolean | `true`           | Specifies whether the Terraform CLI execution passes the `-generate-config-out` flag during the query run. |
| `data.attributes.variables`                       | array[{key, value}] | (empty array) | Specifies an optional list of run-specific variable values. Refer to run-specific variables for details.   |
| `data.relationships.workspace.data.type`          | string  |                  | Must be `"workspaces"`.                                                                                     |
| `data.relationships.workspace.data.id`            | string  |                  | The ID of the workspace to run the query against.                                                          |
| `data.relationships.configuration-version.data.type` | string |               | Must be `"configuration-versions"`.                                                                         |
| `data.relationships.configuration-version.data.id`   | string |               | The ID of the configuration version to use for the query.                                                  |

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only -->
For policy evaluation in HCP Terraform, the request also supports the following optional attributes:

| Key path | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `data.attributes.policy-evaluation-opt-in` | boolean | `true` | Controls automatic workspace policy evaluation. Omission defaults to `true` for every query source. Despite the name, explicit opt-in is not required. Set `false` to suppress automatic workspace policies when query policy opt-out is enabled. |
| `data.attributes.policy-paths` | array of strings | (empty array) | Explicit policy source paths in the uploaded configuration. These paths are independent of the automatic workspace policy preference. Refer to [Explicit policy paths](#explicit-policy-paths). |

### Policy evaluation

Policy evaluation requires a workspace that uses Terraform v1.17.0 or later with remote or agent execution. Terraform v1.17.0-beta2 and later v1.17.0 prereleases also support policy evaluation. Resource discovery alone requires Terraform v1.14.0 or later. Your organization must have Terraform Policy and Search policy evaluation enabled, including access to policy enforcement and versioned policy sets. The execution environment must have a compatible Terraform Policy runtime. Refer to [Search policy requirements](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/import#requirements).

Automatic evaluation uses only applicable Terraform Policy (`tfpolicy`) policy sets targeted for plan-time evaluation, including inherited and organization-wide assignments where applicable. Sentinel, OPA, and sets targeted only at other stages do not participate. Refer to [Policy set configuration](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets/vcs/terraform-policy-vcs#policy-set-configuration-in-hcp-terraform) and [Evaluation stages](/terraform/policy#evaluation-stages).

For API queries, policy evaluation requires `generate-config-out` to be `true`. Terraform evaluates configuration generated from full resource data; identities alone are insufficient. Setting `include_resource = true` in a query definition does not replace the API's generated-configuration requirement. Additional resource reads can increase query duration.

Leave `policy-evaluation-opt-in` omitted to use default evaluation. To query without generated configuration, set both `generate-config-out` and `policy-evaluation-opt-in` to `false`. Explicit opt-out suppresses automatic workspace policies; it does not suppress policies supplied through `policy-paths`.

If no applicable plan-time Terraform Policy sets exist and you provide no explicit policy paths, no policy evaluation occurs. An absent evaluation is not a passing result. Query-time results are informational and do not block import or replace plan-time enforcement.

### Explicit policy paths

Use `policy-paths` to select policy-set directories included in the configuration uploaded for remote execution, for example `["policies/security", "policies/tagging"]`. These are server-side relative paths, not paths to files on your workstation. Each path must:

- Contain between 1 and 255 characters.
- Use only letters, numbers, periods, underscores, dashes, and forward slashes.
- Not start or end with a forward slash or contain `..`.

Explicit paths select policy sources separately from automatic workspace assignments. API policy evaluation still requires generated configuration.
<!-- END: TFC:only -->

### Sample Payload

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only -->
This request omits `policy-evaluation-opt-in`, so HCP Terraform evaluates applicable plan-time Terraform Policy sets by default when the policy prerequisites are met.
<!-- END: TFC:only -->

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "queries",
    "attributes": {
      "source": "tfe-api",
      "generate-config-out": true,
      "variables": [
        { "key": "replicas", "value": "2" }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "workspace": {
        "data": {
          "type": "workspaces",
          "id": "ws-ABC123"
        }
      },
      "configuration-version": {
        "data": {
          "type": "configuration-versions",
          "id": "cv-XYZ789"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Sample Request

```shell
$ curl\
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request POST \
  --data @payload.json \
  https://app.terraform.io/api/v2/queries
```

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only -->
### Sample Payload with policy opt-out

Submit this payload to the same `POST /api/v2/queries` endpoint to generate configuration without evaluating automatic workspace policies:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "queries",
    "attributes": {
      "source": "tfe-api",
      "generate-config-out": true,
      "policy-evaluation-opt-in": false
    },
    "relationships": {
      "workspace": {
        "data": { "type": "workspaces", "id": "ws-ABC123" }
      },
      "configuration-version": {
        "data": { "type": "configuration-versions", "id": "cv-XYZ789" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Policy validation errors

When query policy opt-out is enabled, `policy-evaluation-opt-in` must be a Boolean. For example, supplying the string `"false"` instead of the Boolean `false` returns HTTP `422`:

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "status": "422",
      "title": "invalid attributes",
      "detail": "Policy evaluation opt in must be a boolean"
    }
  ]
}
```

A policy preference of `true` with `generate-config-out: false` also fails validation for API queries because policy evaluation requires generated configuration. Omission uses the default preference of `true`.
<!-- END: TFC:only -->

## List query runs for a workspace

This endpoint lists query runs for a particular workspace.

`GET /workspaces/:workspace_id/queries`

| Parameter        | Description                                           |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `:workspace_id`  | The ID of the workspace to list query runs for.      |

### Query parameters

This endpoint supports pagination [with standard URL query parameters](/terraform/cloud-docs/api-docs#query-parameters). You must use percent-style encoding `[` as `%5B` and `]` as `%5D` if your tooling doesn't automatically encode URLs.

| Parameter      | Description                                                                  |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `page[number]` | Optional. If omitted, the endpoint returns the first page.          |
| `page[size]`   | Optional. If omitted, the endpoint returns 20 query runs per page.  |

| Status  | Response                  | Reason                                                         |
|---------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [200][] | [JSON API document][]     | Successfully retrieved the list of query runs.                 |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][] | Not found or the user is unauthorized to perform this action. |

### Sample Request

```shell
$ curl\
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  https://app.terraform.io/api/v2/workspaces/ws-ABC123/queries
```

## Show a query run

This endpoint shows details for a specific query run.

`GET /queries/:query_id`

| Parameter   | Description                              |
|-------------|------------------------------------------|
| `:query_id` | The ID of the query run to retrieve.     |

| Status  | Response                  | Reason                                                         |
|---------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [200][] | [JSON API document][]     | Successfully retrieved the query run.                          |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][] | Not found or the user is unauthorized to perform this action. |

### Sample Request

```shell
$ curl\
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  https://app.terraform.io/api/v2/queries/query-ABC123
```

## Cancel a query run

This endpoint cancels a query run that is currently pending or running.

`POST /queries/:query_id/actions/cancel`

| Parameter   | Description                          |
|-------------|--------------------------------------|
| `:query_id` | The ID of the query run to cancel.   |

| Status  | Response                  | Reason                                                                |
|---------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [202][] | Empty body                | Successfully canceled the query run.                                  |
| [409][] | [JSON API error object][] | Failed to transition query run to a canceled state.                   |

### Sample Request

```shell
$ curl\
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request POST \
  https://app.terraform.io/api/v2/queries/query-ABC123/actions/cancel
```

## Query run attributes

Query runs have the following attributes:

<!-- BEGIN: TFC:only -->
### Policy attributes

Create, list, and show responses include the persisted `policy-evaluation-opt-in` preference. When Search policy evaluation is enabled for your organization, responses also include `policy-paths`, which is `null` when you provide no explicit paths. These attributes describe the preference and explicit sources, not whether evaluation completes or resources pass.

For the default-evaluation request, the response's `attributes` object includes these additional fields:

```json
{
  "policy-evaluation-opt-in": true,
  "policy-paths": null
}
```

For the opt-out request, the persisted preference is `false`:

```json
{
  "policy-evaluation-opt-in": false,
  "policy-paths": null
}
```

### Policy results in list completions

The show endpoint includes `list-completions` for completed list blocks. When Search policy evaluation is enabled, each entry also includes `policies-passed` and `policies-failed`:

```json
{
  "list-completions": [
    {
      "address": "list.aws_instance.example",
      "resource-type": "aws_instance",
      "total": 5,
      "policies-passed": 3,
      "policies-failed": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

These counts describe resource-row outcomes, not individual policies. They do not need to add up to `total`: a resource can have an unknown result, an evaluation error, or no matching policy. The create and list endpoints do not include `list-completions`.

For detailed policy results and diagnostics, retrieve the existing query log using `log-read-url`. Query results can be incomplete when generated configuration lacks attributes or relationship data that a policy requires. They do not provide a complete compliance assessment or replace plan-time enforcement.
<!-- END: TFC:only -->

### Status

The `status` attribute indicates the current state of the query run. Possible values are:

- `pending`: The query run has been created but is not yet queued for execution.
- `running`: The query run is currently executing.
- `finished`: The query run completed successfully.
- `canceled`: The query run was canceled before completion.
- `errored`: The query run encountered an error during execution.

### Status timestamps

The `status-timestamps` object contains timestamps for when the query run entered each status:

- `pending-at`: When the query run was created.
- `queued-at`: When the query run was queued for execution.
- `running-at`: When the query run started executing.
- `finished-at`: When the query run completed successfully.
- `errored-at`: When the query run encountered an error.
- `canceled-at`: When the query run was canceled.

### Log read URL

The `log-read-url` attribute contains a URL to retrieve the logs for the query run.

## Available Related Resources

The GET endpoints above can optionally return related resources, if requested with the [`include`](/terraform/cloud-docs/api-docs#inclusion-of-related-resources) query parameter. The following resource types are available:

- `created-by` - The user who created the query run.
- `configuration-version` - The configuration version used for the query run.
- `configuration_version.ingress_attributes` - The ingress attributes for the configuration version used for the query run.
